newsitem.title: USA: Pork exports remain strong, add to hog value - NPPC.
newsitem.headline: Pork exports remain strong, add to hog value - NPPC.

text.p: U.S. pork producers continue to benefit from strong pork exports which have added more than $2 per hundred lbs (cwt) to the value of hogs, according to the National Pork Producers Council.
The favorable export/import ratio has added at least $2.25 to $2.50 per cwt to cash hog prices, said University of Missouri economist Glenn Grimes, in the NPPC release.
The positive U.S. pork trade ratio equals between $258 million and $287 million in total gross gain to producers, a $2 billion economic impact on pork the past 10 years, Grimes said.
"Foreign market development is one of the keys to meeting our goal of making pork the Meat of Choice," said Bob Ruggles, President of NPPC.
U.S. pork exports at 534 million lbs, leaped 40 percent during the first six months of 1996, compared with the same period a year earlier, NPPC said.

At the same time, pork imports dropped 12 percent. As a result, the United States is maintaining its status as a net pork exporter, which was established during 1995 for the first time in more than 43 years.
U.S. pork exports to Japan were up 97 percent compared with the same period in 1995, while exports to Canada increased by 113 percent compared to 1995, Grimes added.

The NPPC said the improvement in pork trade since 1985 coincided with the introduction of the national pork legislative checkoff in that year. Over the 10-year period, $10.2 million in producer checkoff funding has been allocated to foreign market development.
